learningOutcomes.description: Recognise and describe number and shape patterns, including triangular, square and power sequences.
Relate visual shape sequences to corresponding number sequences.
Explain simple relationships among number sequences using examples from the chapter.
Identify and distinguish points, line segments, lines, rays and angles.
Compare and classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or reflex.
Measure and draw angles using a protractor.
Use digit patterns, supercells, palindromes and number sequences to investigate numbers.
Apply the Kaprekar routine, estimation strategies and simple number-pattern rules.
Describe and test the Collatz conjecture for given starting numbers.
Collect, organise and interpret data using frequency tables.
Read and interpret pictographs and bar graphs.
Construct and critique bar graphs using suitable scales and orientations.
Find common multiples and common factors and identify prime and co-prime numbers.
Express numbers as products of prime factors.
Apply divisibility tests and use remainders to reason about numbers.
Find the perimeter of polygons and other closed plane figures.
Calculate areas of rectangles, squares, triangles and composite figures using decomposition.
Solve practical problems involving perimeter and area.
Interpret fractions as equal shares, parts of a whole and fractional units.
Compare and find equivalent fractions and convert between improper and mixed fractions.
Add and subtract fractions using common denominators and Brahmagupta's method.
Use a ruler and compass to explore and construct squares and rectangles.
Investigate properties of rectangles and squares, including diagonals and angles.
Construct figures and identify points equidistant from two given points.
Identify lines of reflection symmetry in plane figures.
Determine rotational symmetry and the smallest angle or order of symmetry.
Relate symmetry properties to regular polygons and familiar figures.
Represent positive and negative quantities and integers on a number line.
Add and subtract integers using number lines and token models.
Compare and order integers in contexts involving height, sea level and years.
Describe science as a way of observing, questioning and explaining the world.
Identify observation, questioning, prediction and investigation as parts of scientific inquiry.
Use simple everyday situations to frame questions and suggest ways to investigate them.
Group plants using seed type, roots, venation and other observable features.
Group animals using movement, body features and habitat.
Explain how adaptations and biodiversity relate to different habitats and human actions.

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

learningOutcomes.description: Identify major nutrients and relate them to their functions and food sources.
Use simple tests for starch and fats and interpret observations.
Explain the importance of a balanced diet, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water for health.
Identify magnetic and non-magnetic materials and the two poles of a magnet.
Describe attraction, repulsion and the north-south alignment of a freely suspended magnet.
Use magnets and simple magnetic arrangements to investigate magnetic behaviour.
Measure length using standard units and suitable measuring instruments.
Convert between common units of length and estimate/measures dimensions.
Describe motion relative to a reference point and distinguish linear, circular and oscillatory motion.
Recognise matter and classify materials using observable properties.
Classify materials as transparent, translucent or opaque and as soluble or insoluble in water.
Select materials for objects by considering properties such as hardness, lustre, flexibility and interaction with water.
Distinguish temperature from the sensation of hotness or coldness.
Read laboratory and clinical thermometers and identify their ranges and least counts.
Convert between Celsius and Fahrenheit for values used in the chapter and interpret temperature observations.

chapters.title: A Journey through States of Water

learningOutcomes.description: Describe water in solid, liquid and gaseous states and the changes between them.
Explain evaporation, condensation and cooling in everyday situations.
Relate the water cycle and responsible water use to observations of water in the environment.

chapters.title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

learningOutcomes.description: Explain why mixtures are separated and select suitable separation methods.
Distinguish methods such as handpicking, sieving, filtration, decantation and evaporation.
Relate separation methods to particle size, solubility, density and practical situations.
Identify essential characteristics of living beings and distinguish living from non-living objects.
Describe plant, mosquito and frog life cycles and major stages.
Plan simple investigations involving germination, growth, respiration or response to conditions.
Identify air, water, soil, sunlight, forests and minerals as natural resources.
Distinguish renewable and non-renewable resources and explain responsible use.
Explain how human activities affect forests, soil, air and water and propose conservation actions.
Identify the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, satellites and constellations in the Solar System context.
Recognise patterns such as Orion, the Big Dipper, Little Dipper and the Pole Star.
Explain simple observations of the night sky and the apparent daily motion of celestial objects.
Identify and describe the Earth as a globe and explain the use of maps and globes for locating places.
Explain the concepts of directions, latitude, longitude, the Equator, and the Prime Meridian in locating places on Earth.
Use coordinates, directions, symbols, and scales on maps to locate and describe places.
Interpret basic maps and relate the location of places to their position on the Earth.
Identify the major oceans and continents of the Earth and locate them on a world map.
Describe the distribution of land and water on Earth and distinguish between oceans, seas, and other major water bodies.
Explain selected characteristics and geographical significance of the major oceans and continents.
Interpret maps and geographical information to identify relationships between continents, oceans, and human activity.
Identify major landforms such as mountains, plateaus, and plains and describe their characteristic features.
Explain how landforms influence climate, vegetation, water availability, settlements, and livelihoods.
Compare ways in which people adapt their lives and activities to different landforms.
Interpret maps, illustrations, and examples to relate physical landscapes to human life.
Explain the meaning of history and the importance of studying the past to understand human societies.
Arrange historical events and periods in chronological order using timelines.
Identify different types of historical sources, including archaeological, literary, material, and visual sources.
Use and interpret historical sources to gather evidence about people, places, and events of the past.
Identify the geographical setting of India and describe the significance of the names India, Bharat, and related historical references.
Describe important geographical features that have shaped the development and interactions of the Indian subcontinent.
Explain how geographical and cultural features contributed to connections and continuities across the Indian subcontinent.
Interpret historical and geographical references to understand the evolving idea of India and Bharat.
Describe major features of the Harappan, Indus, or Indus-Sarasvati Civilisation using archaeological evidence.
Identify features of Harappan settlements, including town planning, buildings, drainage, crafts, trade, and material culture.
Explain what archaeological remains and artefacts reveal about the lives, occupations, technologies, and practices of people in the civilisation.
Interpret maps, artefacts, archaeological sites, and other evidence to understand the geographical spread and characteristics of the civilisation.
Identify major ideas, practices, traditions, and knowledge systems that contributed to India's cultural heritage.
Describe selected developments in Indian philosophical, spiritual, scientific, artistic, and literary traditions.
Explain how cultural traditions and knowledge systems have been transmitted, adapted, and preserved across generations.
Recognise connections among different strands of Indian cultural heritage and relate them to contemporary life.

chapters.title: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One'

learningOutcomes.description: Identify forms of diversity in India, including differences in languages, customs, food, clothing, arts, beliefs, and ways of life.
Explain how diverse communities and traditions can coexist while sharing common cultural connections.
Describe examples of cultural exchange, interaction, and shared traditions that illustrate unity in diversity.
Interpret examples from different regions and communities to appreciate the relationship between diversity and social unity.
Describe the family as an important social institution and identify different forms and roles of families.
Explain the meaning of community and describe how communities are formed around shared spaces, activities, relationships, or interests.
Identify ways in which family and community provide support, cooperation, care, and a sense of belonging.
Compare examples of family and community life and recognise how social relationships contribute to collective well-being.
Explain the meaning of governance and identify why societies require systems and institutions for collective decision-making.
Describe key features and principles of democracy, including participation, equality, representation, and accountability.
Explain the relationship between citizens, government, rules, rights, responsibilities, and public institutions.
Identify examples of governance in everyday life and distinguish between individual and collective decision-making.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

learningOutcomes.description: Explain the purpose of local government in rural areas and its role in addressing local needs.
Identify the main institutions and levels of the Panchayati Raj system and describe their functions.
Describe the role of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat in local participation and decision-making.
Explain how rural local bodies undertake development and provide public services through local governance.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

learningOutcomes.description: Explain the purpose of urban local government and its importance in managing towns and cities.
Identify different forms of urban local bodies and describe their broad responsibilities.
Describe how elected representatives and local officials contribute to urban administration and public services.
Relate common urban issues and services to the responsibilities of local government.
Identify different types of work and activities performed by people in households, communities, and workplaces.
Distinguish between paid and unpaid work and recognise the economic and social value of both.
Explain how different forms of work contribute to families, communities, and the wider economy.
Recognise the importance of dignity of labour and equitable appreciation of different kinds of work.
Identify different economic activities and classify examples of production, distribution, exchange, and consumption.
Explain how goods and services are produced and exchanged to meet people's needs and wants.
Describe the roles of workers, producers, consumers, markets, and other participants in economic life.
Interpret everyday examples of economic activity and explain how they are connected through the exchange of goods, services, and money.
